The question is most of the greats across history were not Jewish; the domination by Jews of various industries is a relatively new phenomenon. Is it possible that their creativity and power result from political shifts in education in the Bible? This is a really good criticism of my previous lecture, and maybe there's certain aspects of Jewish culture making them dominant in an industrial capitalistic globalized world. Being materialistic, being capitalist isn't enough; you also need to have an element of creativity within your culture. The Bible helps us better understand the success of Jews. This class is on intellectual speculation—we're trying to figure out theories and play with ideas. Take everything I say with a grain of salt, doubt whatever I say.

So today we will look more closely at why Jews are so dominant. We will explore the argument that Israel and Jewish identity are constructs of imperial imagination. Because of its geographic location, Israel has always been historically imported, and different empires have tried to manipulate the identity of Israel to best promote their own agenda or policies. This is a hard concept to understand, but we'll go slowly.

Last week, we looked at cultures emerging from the project collapse that will dominate history: Greeks, Persians, and Israelites. To understand how these ideas play out in history, we first need to grasp how history works. I've identified three patterns of geopolitics:

1. Competition within nation states matters; competition between them doesn't significantly impact conflict.
2. The elite have shifting loyalties; think of Game of Thrones—everyone wants to be king and will kill family members to achieve it.
3. War can be a mechanism to protect the status quo; conflict is bad, so start wars to maintain equilibrium within your system.

These ideas will guide our discussion throughout the semester. An example: Think of China's war states period before the emergence of the first empire.
